headline: High: shared-file and browser-enabled agent A can inject or leak content into B’s workflows; B’s local-only posture limits exfiltration but not cascading misuse.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A can run browsers, spawn subprocesses, and use runtime-injected MCPs/hooks, so it can ingest untrusted content and present it to Agent B if they share files or copied outputs. Agent B has no documented parsing defenses or isolation. The pairwise pathway is plausible, but shared-channel use is not explicitly documented, so I choose medium over low.
conditions: IF Agent A writes browser-derived content into a shared workspace that Agent B reads
IF Agent B treats Agent A output as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable shared clipboard/file handoff between the agents
Require provenance tags on any A-generated text before B consumes it
Run B in a separate workspace directory
Add a manual review step for any A-sourced instructions
requires-engineering: enforce content-type filtering on MCP and hook inputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A touches project code, session history, and provider authentication data and has broad network egress; Agent B has no network egress and no data classes listed. If they share a workspace, A can expose sensitive local artifacts to external services, while B can still surface A-derived content. The shared-workspace pathway is plausible but not proven, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Agent A and Agent B share a filesystem or copied workspace
IF Agent A sends workspace contents to external APIs during normal operation
mitigations: Keep A and B on separate workspaces
Remove secrets from any shared project tree
Restrict A’s network egress to approved domains
Rotate provider auth data before pairing
requires-engineering: add per-agent data-loss-prevention controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A has broad network egress and subprocess execution, while Agent B is documented with no network egress and no write surfaces. There is no evidence of overlapping mutable resources or shared locks, so direct capability conflict is limited. Uncertainty remains because B’s IO surfaces are empty rather than explicitly read-only, so I keep this at low rather than none.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable directory
IF Agent B is later configured with write-capable integrations
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Avoid concurrent edits to the same repo
Serialize any file-modifying steps
Document which agent owns each resource
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent A can generate browser- and tool-derived outputs, and Agent B’s profile does not show verification or critique behavior. That makes it plausible that B could treat A’s output as authoritative in a workflow chain. The blast radius is multiple work products rather than immediate irreversible harm, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF Agent B consumes Agent A output as input without a validation step
IF Agent A’s browser-derived facts are used to drive downstream actions
mitigations: Insert a human verification step before B acts on A output
Require citations for any factual claims from A
Limit A to drafting, not executing, downstream actions
Flag uncited claims for review
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are docs-only open-source agents, and neither profile documents regulated-data handling, residency, or retention obligations. Agent A does touch provider auth data, but Agent B lists no sensitive data classes and no compliance mismatch is documented. Because the relevant compliance pathway is not evidenced, I keep this low rather than medium.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into Agent A’s workspace
IF Agent B is later configured to process the same regulated data class
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared workspaces
Review vendor/data-processing terms before deployment
Separate logs and retention settings per agent
Document data-class handling for each agent
requires-engineering: implement residency and retention policy enforcement
